name: Talen Energy

logo.source: talenenergy.com site header logo (talen-logo-white.png, 300x91, white wordmark on transparent; no Wikipedia or Commons logo exists). Saved composited on near-black (#0B0B0B) with padding, 380x171, because the official mark is white and would vanish on a light page

description: Talen owns and runs about 13.1 GW of power plants in the US (as of the FY2025 10-K), mostly in the PJM grid region of the Mid-Atlantic and Ohio, plus a share of Colstrip in Montana. The anchor is a 90% interest in the 2.5 GW Susquehanna nuclear plant, which supplies about half its generation, around 17 TWh in 2025 at an all-in cost of about $27 per MWh. It sells electricity and capacity into wholesale markets and has begun locking in long-term contracts: a fixed-price deal to supply up to 1,920 MW of Susquehanna power to an adjacent Amazon Web Services data center campus through 2042, and fixed reliability payments for two Maryland coal plants to May 2029. It is growing by buying gas plants (2.8 GW added in late 2025 and 2.6 GW more in June 2026) and is buying back stock heavily.

gics.note: Wikipedia 'List of S&P 400 companies', raw wikitext read 2026-10-27: Talen Energy, Utilities, Independent Power Producers & Energy Traders (joined the S&P MidCap 400 in 2025, per the same page's change log). That list gives only sector and sub-industry, so industry group and industry are left null rather than recalled from memory.

hq.note: Cover page of the FY2025 10-K: 2929 Allen Pkwy, Suite 2200, Houston, TX 77019

employees.note: Approximately 1,880 full-time employees, about 43% represented by unions (FY2025 10-K, Human Capital)

businessLines.name: PJM segment
businessLines.how: Sells electricity and ancillary services into PJM's day-ahead and real-time markets, sells capacity into PJM auctions years ahead (priced per MW-day), and hedges 60-80% of the next 12 months of generation. Two growing pieces are contracted: AWS buys Susquehanna power at a fixed price under a long-term contract, and the two RMR plants get fixed monthly payments for staying open. The nuclear plant also gets the federal nuclear production tax credit.
businessLines.description: Generation, marketing and fuel management in the PJM market: Susquehanna nuclear plus Talen's natural gas and coal plants in PJM. Includes the AWS contract and the Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner reliability-must-run (RMR) arrangements.

operatingProfit.note: FY2024 PJM Adjusted EBITDA $775M. The note's flattened table did not show an Adjusted EBITDA figure for the Other segment, so no share of a total is computed.

businessLines.name: Other (Colstrip in WECC and other activities)
businessLines.how: Colstrip power is sold through bilateral contracts to buyers in Montana's NorthWestern balancing authority (WECC has no organised energy or capacity market).
businessLines.description: Talen Montana's share of the Colstrip coal plant in the WECC West market, plus small operating and development activities; prior years include the Nautilus bitcoin operation (suspended October 2024) and Texas plants (sold May 2024).

brands.name: Susquehanna nuclear station (Pennsylvania)
brands.share: 2.5 GW; Talen owns 90%; about half of annual generation (about 17 TWh in 2025)

brands.name: Freedom and Guernsey combined-cycle gas plants (acquired November 2025)
Cornerstone portfolio: Waterford (875 MW), Darby (456 MW) in Ohio and Lawrenceburg (1,120 MW) in Indiana (acquired June 15, 2026)
brands.share: About 2.6 GW; purchase price $3.5 billion (cash plus 2,400,000 shares)

brands.name: Brunner Island and Montour (converted coal to gas) and other gas units
brands.share: 4.6 GW intermediate and peaking fleet including 2.9 GW at these two

brands.name: Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner (coal, RMR)
Colstrip (Montana) minority stake
brands.share: Part of about 800 MW of minority coal interests

whatsNext.text: Terry Nutt (President, previously CFO) becomes CEO on January 1, 2027; Mac McFarland stays CEO through December 31, 2026 and retires as senior adviser in March 2027
$1.5 billion accelerated share repurchase announced September 29, 2026, under the program upsized to $3.0 billion through 2028
AWS power contract moves from the behind-the-meter arrangement to a front-of-the-meter arrangement, with full transition expected in spring 2027 and full contract volume no later than 2032
Brandon Shores and H.A. Wagner RMR arrangements run to May 31, 2029 or until transmission upgrades are in service
